scope: Long forward lexical scans of the resident kvbench fixture, 24-byte keys and 100-byte inline values; static source/disassembly review only.
per_input_tuple: splinterdb_iterator_next delegates through core_range_iterator_next, merge advancement, and btree_iterator_next. On an ordinary same-leaf step, B-tree next increments idx, checks entry bounds/message fields and reconstructs a compressed key suffix. It does not acquire or release a cache reference.

btree_iterator_curr exposes the prevalidated entry. It calls cache_validate_page when the leaf is pinned, but release clockcache_validate_page is a single ret, unchanged across all variants. The existing virtual dispatch may remain but it does not perform address or allocator checks.
Merged branches may advance several input tuples per output tuple for duplicate/update histories. There is no fixed input/output multiplier without measuring fixture contents.
cache_work: Each ordinary forward B-tree leaf transition releases the old pinned page and calls synchronous cache_get once for its successor; copied mutable leaves release the newly acquired reference after the page copy. Terminal upper-bound preparation can perform extra tree lookups.

Range initialization and trunk-span rebuilding initialize each participating branch asynchronously. Root-to-leaf positioning and endpoint positioning therefore incur async cache gets at setup/span boundaries.

Extent prefetch checks occur when approaching/crossing an extent boundary, with metadata cursor cache_get(nonblocking) calls on metadata-page acquisition. Successful resident prefetch touches each page mapping/refcount in the prefetched extent. These are not per-tuple address checks.

The invalid-address branch changes prefetch rejection and adds an initial endpoint shape check before existing allocator validation. Per-page prefetch lookup still uses the shared central shape check. Precise prefetch counts are needed in addition to demand-hit counts.
Blob-valued scans can acquire blob pages during materialization per output value. The current 100-byte values are inline, so that exception does not describe this fixture.
attribution: The measured extra 4 sync/8 async hit instructions are amortized over leaves and iterator setup, not paid for every tuple. A 2 percent long-scan loss cannot be assigned directly to those counts without measuring hits, leaves, branch fan-in and prefetch work.

B-tree/core source is identical between main and original. Nine inspected release symbols, including next/curr/check_current/decode_current/next_leaf/core span-next and cache_validate_page hooks, have identical instruction sequences after normalizing absolute and RIP-relative addresses across main/original/sequential.
The evidence leaves runtime placement/layout effects and measurement drift plausible; it does not prove either explanation or establish a numeric upper bound on cache overhead.
targeted_diagnostics_if_loss_repeats: Run an untimed fixed-count replay with use_stats enabled, reset after warmup, then report cache hits/misses by page type and prefetch counters divided by consumed tuples. Keep this separate from performance acceptance measurements.

To distinguish sync versus async and branch leaf versus setup work, use a diagnostic build with thread-local counters at get entry, async first entry, next_leaf and init_span. Count prefetch requests/pages and metadata BUSY separately; avoid shared atomics in counters.

Use perf sampling on the unchanged performance build to compare hot instruction/cycle fractions in B-tree next/check_current/decode, merge advancement, cache get and prefetch. If code sequences remain equal, inspect IPC/frontend stalls/branch misses before changing source.
formatting: Sequential read-only clang-format-19 found one alignment error at original variant line421. Root created formatted candidate with the required spacing before final validation.
